cards.explanation: The answer is the servants who stand in His house. The psalm says, "Give praise, O servants of the LORD, who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God." (Psalm 135:1-2) These are the folks already standing right there in His house. I like that, friends, because showing up is half the job. The other half is not hitting snooze.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "Hallelujah, for the LORD is good…" (Psalm 135:3) That "for" is the psalm handing everybody the reason. It could have said "just do it," but it tells you why. I like a teacher who explains himself, and I'd know.

The answer is His treasured possession. Here's the verse: "For the LORD has chosen Jacob as His own, Israel as His treasured possession." (Psalm 135:4) The psalm calls Israel treasured, not tolerated, not put up with. TREASURED. That's the kind of word you'd want said about you.

The answer is above. The psalm writer says, "For I know that the LORD is great; our Lord is above all gods." (Psalm 135:5) Not next to them, not in the lineup. Above ALL of them. Nobody is even close.

The answer is False. The psalm says the LORD does all that pleases Him "…in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and in all their depths." (Psalm 135:6) The deep seas are on the list, friends. No spot is too far down for Him.

The answer is True. The psalm says He "…brings forth the wind from His storehouses." (Psalm 135:7) Storehouses, like the wind is kept somewhere ready to go. Meanwhile I can't keep the flour from blowing all over my own counter.

The answer is firstborn. The psalm says, "He struck down the firstborn of Egypt, of both man and beast." (Psalm 135:8) This is a heavy part, friends, and I think it's worth slowing down for. The psalm is looking back at what the LORD did in Egypt.

The answer is that He gave it to Israel as an inheritance. The psalm says, "He gave their land as an inheritance, as a heritage to His people Israel." (Psalm 135:12) An inheritance is a gift handed down, not something you earn at the register. The land went to His people.

The answer is False. The psalm says, "Your name, O LORD, endures forever, Your renown, O LORD, through all generations." (Psalm 135:13) All generations, one after the next, not just one. His name doesn't wear out.
The answer is compassion. The psalm says, "For the LORD will vindicate His people and will have compassion on His servants." (Psalm 135:14) That's a tender word, friends. I'll take it.

The answer is people with their own hands. The psalm says, "The idols of the nations are silver and gold, made by the hands of men." (Psalm 135:15) People made them. Imagine a thing that needs YOU to make it, and then can't even speak.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "…they have ears, but cannot hear…" (Psalm 135:17) Ears on the outside, nothing on the inside. That's one expensive pair of decorations.

The answer is that they become like them. The psalm says, "Those who make them become like them, as do all who trust in them." (Psalm 135:18) After that list of mouths that can't speak and ears that can't hear, that lands hard. I'd say that's a warning worth hearing.

The answer is the house of Aaron. The psalm says, "O house of Israel, bless the LORD; O house of Aaron, bless the LORD…" (Psalm 135:19) Aaron's house comes right after Israel's. The roll call is just getting started.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "O house of Levi, bless the LORD; you who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!" (Psalm 135:20) That last call goes to everyone who fears the LORD. The roll call ends with a door held wide open.

The answer is Jerusalem. The psalm says, "Blessed be the LORD from Zion—He who dwells in Jerusalem." (Psalm 135:21) That's the last blessing before the closing Hallelujah, friends. That's a good ending.
